roopkund.title: Why Did Mediterranean Travellers Die in a Himalayan Lake? 💀
roopkund.desc:
Every summer, as the snow melts, Roopkund lake in Uttarakhand (more than 5,000 m up) reveals the remains of hundreds of people. For decades they were thought to have died together in one disaster. In 2019, an international team read the ancient DNA of 38 skeletons: 23 had South Asian ancestry and date to around 800 CE, while 14 had ancestry closest to people of present-day Greece and Crete and date to around 1800 CE, about a thousand years later. The earlier group may have been pilgrims (the lake lies near the route of the Nanda Devi Raj Jat), but no record explains how the later travellers got there.

Sources:
- Harney, É. et al. (2019). Ancient DNA from the skeletons of Roopkund Lake reveals Mediterranean migrants in India. Nature Communications 10, 3670. doi:10.1038/s41467-019-11357-9
- Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History / Harvard Medical School press releases, August 2019
